text: Supervised learning algorithms map input features to continuous or categorical target labels using labeled data.
Unsupervised learning finds hidden patterns and intrinsic structures in unlabeled datasets.
Decision trees split features iteratively based on information gain or Gini impurity.
Random forests construct an ensemble of decorrelated decision trees using bootstrap aggregating.
Support Vector Machines find an optimal hyperplane maximizing the geometric margin between classes.
K-means clustering partitions observations into k distinct clusters by minimizing inertia.
Gradient descent updates model parameters in the opposite direction of the gradient of the loss function.
The bias-variance tradeoff balances model underfitting and overfitting to minimize generalization error.
K-fold cross-validation estimates out-of-sample performance by training on subsets and testing on holds.
Feature scaling like standardization and min-max normalization prevents gradient instability.
Linear regression models the relationship between dependent scalar variables and explanatory features.
Logistic regression applies the sigmoid function to model the probability of binary outcomes.
Regularization techniques such as L1 Lasso and L2 Ridge penalize large regression coefficients.
Principal Component Analysis reduces dimensionality by projecting onto orthogonal eigenvectors.
Evaluation metrics for classification include accuracy precision recall F1-score and ROC-AUC curve.
Natural language processing enables computers to understand interpret and manipulate human language.
Tokenization breaks running text into smaller semantic units such as words subwords or characters.
Stemming and lemmatization reduce inflected words to their root or dictionary canonical base forms.
Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency reflects how important a word is to a document in a collection.
Word2Vec and GloVe learn continuous dense vector representations capturing semantic relationships between words.
Named Entity Recognition identifies and categorizes key information elements such as persons and places.
Part-of-speech tagging assigns grammatical categories like nouns verbs and adjectives to tokens.
Sentiment analysis classifies the emotional polarity and subjective opinion expressed in text.
N-gram language models predict the probability of the next word given a sequence of previous tokens.
Stop words removal filters out frequent functional words like the is at which add little lexical value.
Text summarization generates concise informative summaries using extractive or abstractive approaches.
Byte pair encoding constructs a subword vocabulary by iteratively merging frequent character pairs.
Corpus preprocessing involves casing normalization punctuation stripping and regex cleaning.
Semantic similarity measures cosine distance between contextualized sentence embeddings.
Information retrieval matches user queries against indexed documents using lexical BM25 ranking.
Linear algebra explores vector spaces linear transformations matrices and systems of equations.
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors satisfy the characteristic equation where matrix transformation scales the vector.
Matrix multiplication requires the inner dimensions of the matrices to match.
The determinant of a square matrix indicates whether the system has a unique non-trivial solution.
Differential calculus studies rates of change slopes of curves and tangent lines via derivatives.
Integral calculus calculates accumulated quantities areas under curves and continuous volumes.
The chain rule computes the derivative of composite functions by multiplying individual derivatives.
Partial derivatives measure the rate of change of a multivariable function along specific coordinate axes.
Probability theory studies random phenomena sample spaces conditional likelihoods and events.
Bayes theorem relates the conditional probability of an event given prior evidence and likelihood.
A normal distribution is a continuous symmetric bell-shaped probability distribution defined by mean and variance.
Expectation and variance quantify the central tendency and spread of random variables.
Singular Value Decomposition factorizes any real matrix into unitary and diagonal components.
Gradient vectors point in the direction of steepest ascent of a scalar field.
Hypothesis testing evaluates statistical significance through null hypotheses p-values and z-scores.
Deep learning architectures use multiple layers of nonlinear processing units to model complex abstractions.
Artificial neural networks consist of interconnected input hidden and output neuron layers.
Backpropagation computes gradients of the loss function with respect to weights using the chain rule.
Convolutional neural networks use kernel filters pooling and stride to extract spatial visual patterns.
Recurrent neural networks process sequential data by maintaining internal hidden states across time steps.
Long Short-Term Memory networks solve vanishing gradients using input forget and output gates.
Gated Recurrent Units simplify LSTM architecture by combining forget and input gates into an update gate.
Activation functions like ReLU Sigmoid and Leaky ReLU introduce essential non-linearity into networks.
Dropout randomly deactivates a fraction of neurons during training to prevent co-adaptation and overfitting.
Batch normalization stabilizes neural network training by normalizing activations across mini-batches.
Optimization algorithms like Adam RMSProp and SGD adapt learning rates for fast convergence.
Vanishing and exploding gradients hinder training of deep neural networks across many layers.
Autoencoders learn efficient low-dimensional data encodings in an unsupervised bottleneck manner.
Generative Adversarial Networks train a generator and discriminator network in a zero-sum game.
Residual networks employ skip connections to enable training of extremely deep neural models.
Large language models are autoregressive neural models trained on massive corpora of text.
The Transformer architecture relies entirely on self-attention mechanisms without recurrent connections.
Multi-head self-attention computes scaled dot-product attention across multiple representation subspaces.
Positional encodings inject token order information into permutation-invariant transformer layers.
Prompt engineering optimizes input instructions few-shot examples and system prompts for LLM outputs.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhances LLM responses by retrieving relevant external document chunks.
Fine-tuning adapts pre-trained foundation models on domain-specific datasets using parameter-efficient methods.
Low-Rank Adaptation LoRA freezes base weights and trains lightweight low-rank decomposition matrices.
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback aligns language models with human preferences and safety.
Context window limits define the maximum number of prompt and generation tokens an LLM can process.
Hallucination refers to LLMs generating factually incorrect or ungrounded statements with high confidence.
Chain-of-thought prompting guides language models through intermediate logical steps to solve complex queries.
Temperature and top-p nucleus sampling control the randomness and diversity of model generations.
Quantization reduces memory requirements by converting float16 weights into 8-bit or 4-bit integers.
Vector embeddings map text passages into high-dimensional semantic spaces for semantic similarity lookup.
